title: Usage tier transition, billing grace windows, and rollback rules PRD
creator: Aisha Raman
description: This PRD defines behavior and acceptance criteria for automatic and manual transitions between usage tiers, grace window semantics for quota overages, and safe rollback mechanisms for billing tier changes. The goal is to reduce unexpected charges, provide predictable user experience during temporary spikes, and enable operations to revert tier changes when regressions or billing disputes occur.
background: Multiple customers reported surprise charges from immediate tier promotions during short traffic spikes. Current system immediately upgrades plan entitlements when thresholds are crossed, with no temporary soft-grace period or automated rollback. Infra has limited tooling to revert promotions without manual accounting adjustments. We need rules that balance cost protection, reliability, and operational simplicity.
scope:
IN SCOPE:
- Define thresholds and hysteresis for upward and downward tier transitions
- Implement configurable grace window for short-term overages before billing upgrade
- Provide an automated rollback flow and manual rollback controls in Console
- Emit audit events and billing adjustments for transitions
OUT OF SCOPE:
- Wholesale pricing model changes
- Billing legal contract amendments
- Deep invoice format changes
requirements: R1: Tier transition thresholds must be configurable per plan and include both absolute and rate-based triggers (e.g., tokens/day and tokens/minute)
R2: Grace window feature that delays automatic tier promotion for a configurable period (default 30 minutes) when an overage spike is detected
R3: Soft-notifications to customers during grace window via email/Console banner and usage API webhooks
R4: If usage remains above threshold beyond grace window, automatic tier promotion occurs and billing takes effect from the start of the grace window period
R5: Downward transitions must include stabilization period (hysteresis) to avoid rapid flapping between tiers
R6: Rollback API that marks a recent promotion as reversed, generates a credit line item, and triggers audit logs; rollback must be reversible within 30 days
R7: Console controls for support/ops to approve, schedule, or revert promotions; actions are RBAC-gated and require an approval comment
R8: All transitions must generate structured events for observability and billing reconciliation (event schema documented separately)
R9: Billing calculation details (pro-rata from grace window start) must be surfaced in the billing UI and exported via billing API
R10: Customer-facing communications templates (email, in-app) must be available for both automatic promotions and manual adjustments
acceptance_criteria: AC1: In a simulated sustained spike that exceeds threshold for longer than the grace window, system auto-promotes plan and billing records charge backdated to grace window start; invoices show a single pro-rated line item
AC2: For short spikes that return below threshold within the grace window, no promotion occurs and no billing change is produced
AC3: Support user can execute a rollback on a promotion; rollback generates credit equal to the billed overage and audit entry; customer invoice reflects the credit
AC4: Promotional actions and rollbacks are visible in Console timeline with user, timestamp, reason, and related invoice IDs
AC5: Webhook events for promotions and rollbacks are sent within 30s of action to subscribed endpoints (configurable retry policy applies)
AC6: Metrics dashboard shows promotion counts, average grace window outcomes, number of rollbacks, and total credits issued for the last 90 days
AC7: Unit and integration tests cover threshold triggers, grace-window timing logic, backfill billing calculation, and RBAC authorization flows
dependencies: ENG-23345 (console: timeline and rollback UI components)
PM-19350 (communications: email templates and in-app banners)
FIN-001 (finance: refund and credit policy alignment)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (beta): enable grace window for 10% of accounts with high noise (controlled flag) and monitor metrics for 4 weeks; Phase 2: expand to all self-serve plans and provide opt-out; Phase 3: enable for select enterprise customers with custom thresholds; support team training and runbook published before Phase 2; rollback path validated in staging
notes: Trade-off: longer grace windows reduce customer surprise but increase risk of unpaid sustained overages; default 30 minutes recommended based on usage distributions
Edge case: bursty workloads with repeated short spikes could game grace window; mitigation: implement per-customer spike counter and maximum grace per day
Operational: require a reconciliation job that compares billed promotions to actual usage to detect misbilling within 48h
UX: Console must show an estimated cost impact during a grace window so customers can opt to upgrade proactively
